analysis:
Documentation-only changes; no executable code was supplied.

Units 8d39ffcfaa638a3c:7-9 show head lines 308-752 of docs/reference/configuration.md. According to the range map, none of those lines changed. The changes are the date at line 3 and a new "Add-on hold" section at head lines 149-164, which is visible only in the patch excerpt. I examined the unchanged prefix-cache rows against T-041/SEC-035: the TTL is capped at 1800 s, the KEK fallback (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL) and the DEBUG key file remain documented, and the cache.directory/volume_uuid checks are unchanged. No drift was observed.

The new add-on hold docs describe:
- DARKBLOOM_ADDON_SOCKET, documented as for tests only, with the parent created 0700.
- DARKBLOOM_ADDON_DEV_IDENTITY, documented as read only by DEBUG builds.
- Neither variable is in the LaunchAgent passthrough list.

Unit e0464b5e11a3c520:0 (protocol-messages.md) is metadata only, with no line text. Its patch excerpt adds busy_reason, busy_since_ms and busy_addon to heartbeat/register while status is draining. Those fields expose the holding add-on's code-signing identifier to the coordinator, which is trusted. The hold does not send provider_drain and resumes on the same connection.

Integration questions (unverified, source not supplied):
- Does AddonPeerPolicy.current truly compile out the dev identity in release builds?
- Does AddonHoldPaths reject attacker-controlled socket paths, and how are add-on peers authenticated (TB-003)?
- Does the coordinator exclude providers on register with busy fields? This touches TB-002/T-053 routing and is platform-owned.
- Does a hold that reuses the same connection preserve App Attest grant and endpoint bindings (TB-011/T-053)?

The threat model may need a new entry for the local add-on hold IPC boundary, which is a new local attack surface. Without code, no concrete regression is supported.
